description: Shared firewall contract for odoo_safe_mcp/rules.py (evaluate_odoo_call) and the Guard Worker's src/policy.ts (evaluateRiskOnEdge). Both test suites run every vector; if one engine changes and the other does not, a suite fails. Canonical copy: odoo-safe-mcp/tests/policy_vectors.json; the Worker keeps a byte-identical copy in test/policy_vectors.json (npm run sync:vectors) and both suites compare the two files when the sibling checkout is present.
rules: expected_level uses Python names; FORBIDDEN is 'BLACK' on the Edge (see level_mapping).

expected_sanitized_args / expected_sanitized_kwargs default to the input args / kwargs. They are compared as serialised JSON, so key order matters: the Edge compares JSON.stringify output before signing a draft.

Every YELLOW expectation must be a fixed point: evaluating the sanitised payload again gives YELLOW and the same payload. Otherwise the Edge answers 409 POLICY_MISMATCH to the client's already-sanitised draft.
An 'edge' (or 'python') object overrides expectations for that engine only and must name an intentional difference.
Inputs must never be mutated by the engine.
Not compared: reason and audit_note texts (different languages), Python-only flags (allowed, requires_guard_proxy, inject_chatter_note) and licence gating in evaluate_rule().

intentional_differences.D1: Reads on protected system models (tables.protected_system_models: res.groups, ir.model, ir.ui.view...) are GREEN in Python, which runs them locally, and BLACK on the Edge. Reads never reach the Edge (it answers INVALID_PROXY_CALL to GREEN), so the Edge keeps the stricter blanket block. Mutations on those models are FORBIDDEN in both.
intentional_differences.D2: On GREEN reads Python strips credential-like names from kwargs['fields'] (and redacts the response). The Edge never executes reads, so it returns kwargs unchanged.
